newsitem.title: USA: Agreement frees up U.S. anti-drug aid to Colombia.
newsitem.headline: Agreement frees up U.S. anti-drug aid to Colombia.

text.p: The United States signed a monitoring agreement with Colombia on Friday that will allow the renewal of U.S. anti-drug assistance halted by human rights concerns.

The end-use agreement will allow U.S. officials to carry out inventories to make sure weapons and money supplied to Colombia for the drug war are not being used by military units fighting rebel groups.

"We are very pleased that we are able to conclude this agreement and believe it will strongly promote both our counternarcotics and human rights objectives in Colombia," State Department spokesman James Foley told reporters.

The agreement was signed at the State Department by Acting Assistant Secretary of State for Narcotics and Law Enforcement Affairs Jane Becker and Colombian ambassador to Washington Juan Carlos Esguerra.
Colombia is the world's largest producer of cocaine.

U.S. anti-drug assistance to Colombia was suspended under the Leahy law, named after Sen. Patrick Leahy of Vermont, which banned military aid to Colombian armed forces deemed responsible for human rights violations.
"This agreement allows us to ensure that our assistance conforms to that provision," Foley said.

The agreement will allow the State Department to provide $45 million in anti-drug assistance to Colombia this year and the Pentagon plans to send $40 million in military equipment to the Colombian military and the National Police, Foley said.

The Clinton administration is also discussing with Congress a proposal to provide an additional $30 million in equipment to the National Police, which is responsible for counter-nacotics efforts in Colombia, the spokesman said.
The U.S. government has decertified Colombia for two years for not cooperating sufficiently in fighting the drug trade.
Decertification blocks U.S. aid that is not related to the anti-drug war and requires the United States to vote against loans to Colombia by international financial institutions.
